t: Roman Britain was the province of Britannia, covering most of England and Wales from the Claudian invasion of 43 until about 410.
It held one of the largest garrisons in the empire, guarding a northern frontier marked by Hadrian's Wall and the Antonine Wall.
Towns such as London, York and Lincoln, a road network, villas and Christianity were its lasting legacies.
dyk: Constantine the Great was proclaimed emperor at York in 306, after his father Constantius died there while campaigning in Britain.
ev: Claudius's general Aulus Plautius invades with four legions; Camulodunum falls
Boudica of the Iceni destroys Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium before her defeat
Agricola defeats the Caledonians at Mons Graupius in northern Scotland
Building begins on Hadrian's Wall from the Tyne to the Solway
Carausius declares himself emperor and rules Britain independently until 293
Constantine the Great is proclaimed emperor at York
Picts, Scotti and Saxons overrun the province in the 'barbarian conspiracy'
Honorius reportedly tells the cities of Britain to look to their own defence

f.predecessor: British Iron Age peoples such as the Catuvellauni
f.successor: Sub-Roman British kingdoms such as Powys and Dumnonia
